For \(p>2\), both steps are strict unless \(ab=0\), which supplies the boundary obstruction. Summing coordinatewise proves the necessary condition. Orthogonal complements prove the Hilbert case; a coordinate outside finitely many countable supports proves the uncountable case; coordinate decay plus continuity of the two one-coordinate norm formulas proves the strict countable interior. A full-support unit vector forces failure on the countable boundary. value.rationale: The two-parameter property was introduced specifically to quantify almost squareness, and \(\ell_p(\Gamma)\) is a canonical benchmark family already used by the introducing paper. A complete parameter classification is therefore a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The result reveals a structural phenomenon invisible at the previously displayed diagonal point: for every \(p>2\), the entire boundary \(r^p+s^p=1\) is present for uncountable index sets but absent for separable \(\ell_p\), while \(p=2\) behaves differently because finite sets admit an orthogonal unit direction. This gives a sharp, reusable benchmark for future parametric-ASQ and transfinite comparisons.
